name: S11 (How to use this very large guide, P1)
text: Also read some of the stuff in the daily and weekly sections, to make the practice your own.

name: S12 (The table of contents is hiding on the left, P1)
text: It’ll be really helpful for this guide as it’s a long one.

name: S14 (Protecting Yourself from Hypnotists, P2)
text: There are a lot of ways to influence people without engaging their conscious mind. Marketers and interface designers know this perfectly well. The Federal Trade Commission has a report on “dark patterns” - designs that trick or manipulate consumers.

name: S15 (Protecting Yourself from Hypnotists, P3)
text: Conscious agreement, unconscious receptivity, emotional compliance, legal and ethical consent - can people have their minds influenced without the conscious agreement of their adult self?

name: S16 (Forget the left-brain/right-brain cartoon, P4)
text: So each can correct the other.

name: S17 (Forget the left-brain/right-brain cartoon, P5)
text: It’s got to lead somewhere!

name: S18 (Why doing it myself worked better for me, P1)
text: One reason might have been that I was sober when I did that, and didn’t feel that susceptible to hypnosis. But I think a bigger reason is trust and precision.

name: S19 (Why doing it myself worked better for me, P2)
text: I can tell when my body is saying no, before my conscious mind can twist it around to a yes.

name: S20 (When “your voice” is everybody else’s voice, P11)
text: You want to be able to let the quiet little preferences that you have bubble up to the surface and know for sure that you’re not going by what your social group would want you to do.

name: S21 (Please don’t put six metaphors in one trance, P2)
text: When you’re done, make sure to come back the other way.

name: S22 (Please don’t put six metaphors in one trance, P3)
text: And then read it out loud as you write it. Long, elegant sentences are NOT going to help you when you’re trying to induce. It’s all soup to you at that point.

name: S23 (Before you begin, P2)
text: Think about what you want to do. Are there things you don’t want to do today?

name: S24 (Before you begin, P3)
text: Make sure you’re in a safe place to do this.

name: S25 (Before you begin, P4)
text: Decide to do it. How will you coax yourself to do this? Make it spacious? Make it warm and held? etc. Preview what you are going to do. Will you close your eyes? Will you come out and go back in again? What will you do at the end?

name: S26 (Capacity before content, P8)
text: What is one next thing I can do?

name: S27 (Capacity before content, P9)
text: especially if it has to do with trauma or memories. The mind makes it symbolic, squashes things together, distorts, dramatizes, pulls from cultural influences, fears etc. So take it as an image and get some outside help!

name: S28 (Nothing happens, P1)
text: Could you try this on a smaller scale?

name: S29 (Nothing happens, P2)
text: Maybe ask to be shown just one body sensation, or just one word. Or even just whether today is for listening or resting.

name: S30 (It feels fake, P1)
text: Have you got any sense of what it is that’s making it feel fake?

name: S31 (It feels fake, P2)
text: You may have fooled yourself in the past, and that part remembers.

name: S32 (Pattern 6: Ethical double binds, P2)
text: An Ethical Double Bind Question gives someone a choice between two genuinely safe things to do.

name: S33 (Anxiety script, P1)
text: Here is a little script you could use:

name: S34 (Anxiety script, P2)
text: Let’s see if I can find my body parts.

name: S36 (Forgiveness without bypass, P5)
text: What’s theirs and what’s mine?
